solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Argued about exploit outside club

indicators.note: the word for an exploit is placed outside, around the club

parts.note: an exploit is a deed, a notable act
a bat is a club used in sport

explanation.surface: Someone quarrelled about a daring escapade that took place outside a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' looks like a nightclub, but it is the sporting implement; 'outside' puts the exploit word around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To have debated something is to have discussed or argued it, so the past tense phrase matches.

clue.text: In reality, nasty two-faced women will be shunned

indicators.note: nasty suggests something ugly and twisted, signalling the letters are rearranged
being shunned means kept out, so this letter is removed from the pool

explanation.surface: Actually, spiteful hypocritical women are going to be avoided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' rearranges the letters of TWO-FACED once 'will be shunned' has removed the W for women, leaving OFACED to become DEFACTO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means existing in fact, whether or not legally recognised, so it equals 'in reality'.

clue.text: Singer terrible, always swallowing a couple of lines

indicators.note: swallowing means taking something in, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: terrible means bad
L stands for line, so two lines give LL
E'ER is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A dreadful vocalist keeps on gulping down a few lines of the lyric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallowing' takes A and a couple of lines into the pair of words for terrible and always, just after the first letter. E'ER is poetic for ever.
explanation.definitionFit: A balladeer is a performer of ballads, a kind of singer.

clue.text: Suggestion of rain? Time to run

parts.note: to race is to run fast

explanation.surface: A hint of drizzle in the forecast, so it is time to dash for shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather reports speak of a trace of rain, meaning a very slight amount, a mere hint of it.

clue.text: Conversation is so crude, out of order

indicators.note: out of order means not in the proper sequence, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint that some talk is so vulgar that it is unacceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' looks like a verdict on the crude talk, but it tells you to rearrange IS SO CRUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Discourse is formal spoken or written communication, a synonym for conversation.

clue.text: Two similar coins half way across?

parts.note: a cent is a small coin
a red cent is American slang for a coin of almost no value, so red stands for it

explanation.surface: Two matching coins placed on a line at the midpoint.
explanation.walkthrough: The second coin comes from the US idiom 'not worth a red cent'; both coins are worth next to nothing, and the question mark flags a whimsical definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something placed half way across a space sits in the middle of it, so it is positioned at the midpoint.

clue.text: Profanity comes from scoundrels taking drug

parts.note: curs are contemptible people, rogues
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Swearing is heard from villains who take narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: A curse is a swear word or oath, an instance of profanity.

clue.text: Innovative sort of athletics event in paper

parts.note: something innovative is new
a sprint is a short running race on the track

explanation.surface: A newspaper reports on a novel kind of track and field race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paper' at the end reads as a newspaper, but it is the cheap stock that newspapers are printed on.
explanation.definitionFit: Newsprint is the cheap coarse paper on which newspapers are printed.

clue.text: Cook presents browned bread with new topping

indicators.note: a new topping means the first letter of the word is changed for another

parts.note: toast is bread browned by heat

explanation.surface: A chef offers grilled bread with a fresh topping on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new topping' looks like something spread on toast, but it means the T at its top is replaced; R gives the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To roast is to cook food in an oven or over a fire.

clue.text: A time wasted by grown-up — fat person with little intelligence

indicators.note: wasted means lost or used up, so these letters are taken away

parts.note: a grown-up is an adult
lard is pig fat

explanation.surface: A grown-up wastes time, becoming a fat and dim individual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasted' strips A and the abbreviation for time from the grown-up word, leaving three letters before the fat.
explanation.definitionFit: A dullard is a slow-witted, stupid person.

clue.text: Composer putting everything into two notes

indicators.note: into means the first piece goes inside the second

parts.note: F and A are two notes of the musical scale
all means everything

explanation.surface: A composer fits all his music into just a couple of notes.
explanation.walkthrough: Manuel de Falla was a Spanish composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Manuel de Falla was a twentieth-century Spanish composer, known for ballet music.

clue.text: What spin bowler wants to do as an odd fellow?

definitions.text: What spin bowler wants to do
definitions.meaning: a cricket bowler wants to screw the ball, giving it spin so it turns

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a spin bowler makes the ball turn off the pitch; to screw a ball is to put such spin on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A screwball is slang for an eccentric person; in sport it is a ball delivered with reverse spin.

clue.text: Fellow, one to protect Queen as attendant

indicators.note: protecting means surrounding, so the other pieces go round

parts.note: a chap is a fellow
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A man, a single bodyguard, guards the monarch while waiting on her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to protect' has the fellow and one wrap round the royal cipher of Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperone accompanies and supervises someone, an attendant at a social occasion.

clue.text: Old city type, tramp frayed at the edges

indicators.note: worn away at the edges, so the ends of the run are lost and the middle remains

explanation.surface: A vagrant of a certain sort, ragged around the edges, in an ancient town.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip the outer letters of 'type tramp' (TY and MP) and the middle PETRA remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Petra is the ancient rock-cut city in Jordan, capital of the Nabataeans.

clue.text: Warnings thus rejected, soldiers will be trapped

indicators.note: being trapped means caught inside, so this piece goes within the other
rejected means sent back, so the word is turned around

parts.note: so means thus
men is a common word for soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: Warnings are therefore ignored and the troops end up caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns the word for thus around, and 'will be trapped' puts the soldiers inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Omens are signs foretelling events, often warnings of something bad.

clue.text: Society getting scary — money no longer available

parts.note: chilling means frightening

explanation.surface: Society becomes frightening because the cash has run out.
explanation.walkthrough: The schilling was Austria's currency until the euro replaced it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Austrian schilling was a currency withdrawn when the euro came in, so it is defunct cash.

clue.text: Irritation with mistake — top journalist severely criticised

parts.note: a rub is a source of irritation or difficulty
bish is British slang for a blunder
ED, short for editor, is the senior journalist on a paper

explanation.surface: Irritated by an error, the senior newspaperman tore into the culprit.
explanation.walkthrough: BISH is British slang for a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: To rubbish something is to criticise it harshly or dismiss it as worthless.

clue.text: Desire one found in famous old footballer to be most spiteful

indicators.note: found in means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: George Best was a celebrated Northern Irish footballer
an itch is a restless desire
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A craving was detected in a legendary player who turned out to be the nastiest.
explanation.walkthrough: George Best was a Manchester United star of the 1960s; 'found in' puts the desire and the numeral one inside his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitchy means malicious and spiteful, so the superlative is the most spiteful.

clue.text: The woman's single item of furniture that could be passed to offspring

definitions.text: that could be passed to offspring

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman
I is the Roman numeral one, a single
a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: Her only piece of furniture is something she could leave to her children.
explanation.definitionFit: Heritable means capable of being inherited, transmissible from parent to child.

clue.text: Mum or Dad wrapping children maybe initially in goatskin?

indicators.note: wrapping means enclosing, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: either is a parent

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A parent swaddling the kids, perhaps, in a goat hide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes only the first letter of 'maybe'; 'wrapping' puts it and the children abbreviation inside the parent. The question mark flags goatskin as one example of the material.
explanation.definitionFit: Parchment is writing material made from animal skin, often goat or sheep.

clue.text: Pagan god, star performer with a cure for everything

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of shepherds
an ace is an expert or star

explanation.surface: A heathen deity and a star turn bring a universal remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A panacea is a supposed remedy for all ills.

clue.text: Learners incorporated into duty roster

indicators.note: incorporated into means contained within the following words

explanation.surface: Trainees are added to the work rota.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyros are beginners or novices, people still learning.

clue.text: Poet certainly upset about place of the damned

indicators.note: about means going around, so the other piece is enclosed
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: yes means certainly
hell is where the damned are sent

explanation.surface: A poet, unquestionably distressed, writes about the underworld.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' reads the word for certainly from bottom to top, and 'about' wraps that round the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: Percy Bysshe Shelley was an English Romantic poet.

clue.text: Book of the month starts to excite librarians

parts.note: Nov is the abbreviation for November

indicators.note: starts means take the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: The month's featured title begins to thrill the library staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book of the month' looks like one phrase, but 'Book' is the definition and 'the month' is NOV.
explanation.definitionFit: A novel is a full-length work of fiction, published as a book.

clue.text: Planet ultimately lacking, energy limited — conference here?

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter, and lacking says it is removed

parts.note: Venus is the second planet from the sun

indicators.note: limited means cut down to just its first letter

explanation.surface: A planet running short of power: is this where the meeting is held?
explanation.walkthrough: VENUS loses its last letter and E, energy cut back to one letter, follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A venue is the place where an event such as a conference is held.

clue.text: Flat mate? A techie with BO unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests a mess, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether a technician with body odour would make a suitable flatmate.
explanation.walkthrough: BO is body odour. 'Flat mate' reads as a flatmate, but it means a partner who shares one's home.
explanation.definitionFit: A cohabitee lives with a partner, a mate sharing the flat.

clue.text: Presiding officer in church broadcast

parts.note: to air is to broadcast

explanation.surface: The person in charge at church is put on the airwaves.
explanation.definitionFit: The chair is the person who presides over a meeting.

clue.text: Country's medical organisation outside the old city

indicators.note: outside means placed around the other piece

parts.note: BMA is the British Medical Association, the doctors' professional body
Ur is the ancient city in Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A nation's doctors' body is located beyond the historic town centre.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'. Burma is the former name of Myanmar.
explanation.definitionFit: Burma is the older name for Myanmar, a Southeast Asian nation.

clue.text: Is girl able to go out with a prospective employee?

parts.note: to be able is can
Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
to date someone is to go out with them

explanation.surface: Is a young woman allowed out with a job applicant?
explanation.walkthrough: Read the question as 'Can Di date?', meaning is the girl able to go out.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate is an applicant for a job, someone who may be employed.

clue.text: Stagger to contain British anarchist?

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the letter goes within

parts.note: to reel is to stagger

explanation.surface: Is the Briton lurching about a revolutionary?
explanation.definitionFit: An anarchist is one kind of rebel, someone resisting authority; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: State restricts English person wanting justice through violence?

indicators.note: restricting means confining, so the other piece is held inside

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: A state limiting the English: is this a vigilante?
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a country or US state, but it is the verb AVER.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenger takes revenge, seeking retribution by force for a wrong.

clue.text: Attempt to conceal old event causing great pain

indicators.note: concealing means hiding inside, so the other piece goes within

parts.note: a try is an attempt
aged means old

explanation.surface: Trying to cover up an old incident that caused great suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedy is a disaster or calamity, an event causing great distress.
